resources.string: Lets an administrator in your organisation\'s Argus console touch this device\'s screen during a session you accepted. Argus does not read the screen through this service.
Not linked to an Argus yet
Scan the code from the console

Argus stops: sessions can no longer be opened to this device, unattended control is turned off and its pairing forgotten, and the accessibility service is switched off. What has not reached Argus yet is sent first.
To finish, uninstall the Argus app. If wireless debugging was used, revoke its authorisations in Developer options.
Accessibility service is on: Argus can touch the screen
Accessibility service is off: Argus can watch but not touch
Linked. Finish adding the device in the console.
%1$s wants to watch this device\'s screen.
Everything on the screen is shared and recorded until the session ends. You can stop it at any time from the banner.
%1$s is controlling this device via Argus
%1$s is watching this device via Argus
Attended: someone accepts each session on the device.
Unattended: sessions open with nobody here. Wireless debugging is on.

For a company device with nobody holding it. Turn on Wireless debugging in Developer options, then enter the pairing address and code it shows. This leaves wireless debugging on, which listens on the network; use it only on devices you own.
Argus: an app change to confirm
Your organisation asks to install %1$s. Tap to see Android\'s question.
Your organisation asks to uninstall %1$s. Tap to see Android\'s question.
Installing apps is allowed: Android asks you each time one is installed.
Installing apps is not allowed yet: your organisation cannot install apps here.
